q-333165.name: Question 1
q-333165.problem:
An initial value problem has the exact solution ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ A numerical method is used to approximate the solution to the initial value problem, resulting in the table below, where $y$ denotes the approximate solution at each step, and ${τ}_{n}$ is the local truncation error at each step. At each step, the exact value is used to approximate the new value. 

Calculate the local truncation error at each step. Round your answers to three decimal places.

| $n$ | $x$ | $y$ | ${τ}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.25$ | $0.970$ | {{field-1}} |
| $2$ | $0.5$ | $0.880$ | {{field-2}} |
| $3$ | $0.75$ | $0.735$ | {{field-3}} |
q-333165.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the LTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

- After the first step, we have ${y}_{\text{new}}=0.970.$ So, the LTE of the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{1} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.25)-0.970 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.25)-0.970 \\  & ≈-0.001.\end{aligned}
$$

- After the second step, we have ${y}_{\text{new}}=0.880.$ So, the LTE of the second step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{2} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.5)-0.880 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.5)-0.880 \\  & ≈-0.002.\end{aligned}
$$

- After the third step, we have ${y}_{\text{new}}=0.735.$ So, the LTE of the third step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{3} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.75)-0.735 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.75)-0.735 \\  & ≈-0.003.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $n$ | $x$ | $y$ | ${τ}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $0$ |

q-332884.name: Question 3
q-332884.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={e}^{2x},$ compute the local truncation error ${τ}_{11}$ for the step starting at $x=1$ with step size $Δx=0.1.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

${τ}_{11}≈$
{{field-1}}
q-332884.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={e}^{2x}.$ So, the $y$-value at the start of the step $x=1$ is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(1)={e}^{2}.$

Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1) & =2{y}_{\text{exact}}(1) \\  & =2\cdot {e}^{2} \\  & =2{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1)\cdot Δx \\  & =2{e}^{2}\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.2{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1+0.1) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.1) \\  & ={e}^{2\cdot 1.1} \\  & ={e}^{2.2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the step starting at $x=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{11} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.1)-({y}_{\text{exact}}(1)+Δy) \\  & ={e}^{2.2}-({e}^{2}+0.2{e}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{2.2}-1.2{e}^{2} \\  & ≈0.158\end{aligned}
$$

q-334177.name: Question 4
q-334177.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x+4,\,y(0)=0
$$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{3}({x}^{2}+{y}^{′})\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+4x,$ compute the local truncation error, ${τ}_{6},$ for the step starting at $x=1$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

${τ}_{6}≈$
{{field-1}}
q-334177.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+4x.$ So, the $y$-value at the start of the step $x=1$ is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(1)=5.$

Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1) & =2(1)+4 \\  & =2+4 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{3}({x}^{2}+{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1))\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(1+6)\cdot 0.2 \\  & ≈0.4667.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2) \\  & =(1.2)^{2}+4(1.2) \\  & =6.24\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the step starting at $x=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{6} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2)-({y}_{\text{exact}}(1)+Δy) \\  & =6.24-(5+0.4667) \\  & ≈0.773\end{aligned}
$$

q-333838.name: Question 5
q-333838.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+1,$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$
q-333838.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{2}+1.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+{y}_{\text{exact}}(x))\cdot Δx \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+{x}^{2}+1)\cdot Δx \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)\cdot Δx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & =({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δx) \\  & =(x+Δx)^{2}+1 \\  & ={x}^{2}+2x\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =[{x}^{2}+2x\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2}+1]-[{x}^{2}+1+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)\cdot Δx] \\  & ={x}^{2}-{x}^{2}+1-1+(2x-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1))\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2} \\  & =(2x-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1))\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method: Δy=ln⁡(x+y)⋅Δxynew=y+Δy If the exact solution is yexact(x)=x2+1, find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from x to xnew=x+Δx.

a
(2x−ln⁡(x2+x+1))⋅Δx+(Δx)2
b
(2x−ln⁡(x2+x+1))⋅Δx+2(Δx)2
c
(x−ln⁡(x2+x+1))⋅Δx+(Δx)2
d
(2x−ln⁡(x+x2))⋅Δx+(Δx)2
e
(2x−ln⁡(x2+1))⋅Δx+(Δx)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step n from x with exact value yexact to xnew=x+Δx is

τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=yexact(xnew)−(yexact(x)+Δy).

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is yexact(x)=x2+1. Now, let's find the y-increment given by the numerical method: Δy=ln⁡(x+yexact(x))⋅Δx=ln⁡(x+x2+1)⋅Δx=ln⁡(x2+x+1)⋅Δx

Next, we compute the exact value at xnew: yexact(xnew)=(yexact(x)+Δx)=(x+Δx)2+1=x2+2x⋅Δx+(Δx)2+1

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step n starting at x: τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=[x2+2x⋅Δx+(Δx)2+1]−[x2+1+ln⁡(x2+x+1)⋅Δx]=x2−x2+1−1+(2x−ln⁡(x2+x+1))⋅Δx+(Δx)2=(2x−ln⁡(x2+x+1))⋅Δx+(Δx)2

q-333837.name: Question 6
q-333837.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =(xy+{y}^{2})\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{x}^{2}+5x,$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$
q-333837.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{x}^{2}+5x.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =(x\cdot {y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+{y}_{\text{exact}}(x)^{2})\cdot Δx \\  & =(x\cdot (3{x}^{2}+5x)+(3{x}^{2}+5x)^{2})\cdot Δx \\  & =(3{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+9{x}^{4}+30{x}^{3}+25{x}^{2})\cdot Δx \\  & =(9{x}^{4}+33{x}^{3}+30{x}^{2})\cdot Δx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & =({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δx) \\  & =3(x+Δx)^{2}+5(x+Δx) \\  & =3({x}^{2}+2x\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2})+5x+5(Δx) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+6x\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}+5x+5(Δx) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+5x+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =[3{x}^{2}+5x+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}]-[3{x}^{2}+5x+(9{x}^{4}+33{x}^{3}+30{x}^{2})\cdot Δx] \\  & =3{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+5x-5x+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}-(9{x}^{4}+33{x}^{3}+30{x}^{2})\cdot Δx \\  & =(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}-(9{x}^{4}+33{x}^{3}+30{x}^{2})\cdot Δx \\  & =(-9{x}^{4}-33{x}^{3}-30{x}^{2}+6x+5)\cdot Δx+3(Δx)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method: Δy=(xy+y2)⋅Δxynew=y+Δy If the exact solution is yexact(x)=3x2+5x, find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from x to xnew=x+Δx.

a
(−9x4−33x3−30x2+6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2
b
(x−x3−x4)⋅Δx+(Δx)2
c
(2x−x3)⋅Δx+2(Δx)2
d
(2x−2x3−x4)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2
e
9x4+33x3+30x2+6x+5⋅Δx+3(Δx)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step n from x with exact value yexact to xnew=x+Δx is τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=yexact(xnew)−(yexact(x)+Δy).

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is yexact(x)=3x2+5x. Now, let's find the y-increment given by the numerical method: Δy=(x⋅yexact(x)+yexact(x)2)⋅Δx=(x⋅(3x2+5x)+(3x2+5x)2)⋅Δx=(3x3+5x2+9x4+30x3+25x2)⋅Δx=(9x4+33x3+30x2)⋅Δx

Next, we compute the exact value at xnew: yexact(xnew)=(yexact(x)+Δx)=3(x+Δx)2+5(x+Δx)=3(x2+2x⋅Δx+(Δx)2)+5x+5(Δx)=3x2+6x⋅Δx+3(Δx)2+5x+5(Δx)=3x2+5x+(6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step n starting at x: τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=[3x2+5x+(6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2]−[3x2+5x+(9x4+33x3+30x2)⋅Δx]=3x2−3x2+5x−5x+(6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2−(9x4+33x3+30x2)⋅Δx=(6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2−(9x4+33x3+30x2)⋅Δx=(−9x4−33x3−30x2+6x+5)⋅Δx+3(Δx)2

| $n$ | ${x}_{n}$ | ${y}_{n}$ | ${e}_{n}$ |

| $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.25$ | $1.030$ | {{field-1}} |

$$
{e}_{n}=y({x}_{n})-{y}_{n},
$$

where $y({x}_{n})$ is the exact value at ${x}_{n},$ and ${y}_{n}$ is the numerical value produced after $n$ steps.

We are given the numerical values ${y}_{n}$ produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value $y({x}_{n})$ at each value of ${x}_{n}:$

- The exact value at ${x}_{2}=0.5$ is $y(0.5)=\sqrt{1+(0.5)^{2}}.$

- The exact value at ${x}_{3}=0.75$ is $y(0.75)=\sqrt{1+(0.75)^{2}}.$

$$

EXPLANATION

The global truncation error (GTE) is the total error accumulated after several steps of a numerical method. The GTE of a numerical method at step n from xn−1 to xn=xn−1+Δx is en=y(xn)−yn, where y(xn) is the exact value at xn, and yn is the numerical value produced after n steps.

We are given the numerical values yn produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value y(xn) at each value of xn:

  • The exact value at x0=0 is y(0)=12(0)2+1=1.

  • The exact value at x1=0.2 is y(0.2)=12(0.2)2+1.

  • The exact value at x2=0.4 is y(0.4)=12(0.4)2+1.

  • The exact value at x3=0.7 is y(0.7)=12(0.7)2+1.
